notes.content: This agreement displays all lower-division courses required in the major: CSU Northridge courses on the left, approved (articulated) transfer courses to the right. notes.contentHtml:
This agreement displays all lower-division courses required in the major: CSU Northridge courses on the left, approved (articulated) transfer courses to the right. General education (Cal-GETC or CSU Northridge GE) and upper-division courses are also required to complete the bachelor's degree.


Completion of all coursework listed in this agreement is not mandatory prior to admission. For CSU Northridge Undergraduate Admission Requirements, refer to Upper Division Transfer.


Some coursework may be satisfied by Advanced Placement exams completed in high school. Visit AP Credit for information. Additional information about the major is available in the CSUN University Catalog.


Questions regarding this agreement may be directed to: articulation@csun.edu.

notes.content: Students will choose one of seven possible concentrations: Philosophy and Religion Race and Ethnicity Communication and Media Law and Public Policy Social Work and Welfare Criminology Literature The Concentration Courses listed below are applicable in the following concentrations: Race and Ethnicity Concentration - Contemporary Issues of the Chicana; Gender, Sexuality, and American Indian Communities OR Gender, Sexuality, and American Indian Communities; Race and Ethnicity in Queer Studies Social Work and Welfare Concentration - Women and Health
notes.contentHtml:
Students will choose one of seven possible concentrations:

  1. Philosophy and Religion
  2. Race and Ethnicity
  3. Communication and Media
  4. Law and Public Policy
  5. Social Work and Welfare
  6. Criminology
  7. Literature


The Concentration Courses listed below are applicable in the following concentrations:

  • Race and Ethnicity Concentration - Contemporary Issues of the Chicana; Gender, Sexuality, and American Indian Communities OR Gender, Sexuality, and American Indian Communities; Race and Ethnicity in Queer Studies
  • Social Work and Welfare Concentration - Women and Health
